reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: 1× updateEntityColumn on a scroll position, then channel.flush(); an OIMSingleComputed first visible index over it and one effect on the index
reading.floor: 1× position(v) with no batch; an alien computed first visible index and one alien effect on it
reading.caveat: ONE OPERATION IS 1 WRITE OF A SCROLL POSITION AND ONE SETTLE. A derived first visible index, floor(position / 32), sits on the position and one effect reads the index, so the position changes on every write and the index once per 32 writes: the effect body runs once per 32 pixels on both arms. THE SAME-VALUE STATEMENT BELOW HOLDS FOR THE POSITION AND NOT FOR THE INDEX: the index is stopped by each arm's own equality check (the default sameValueGuard of OIMSingleComputed, and alien's computed comparison), which is what this row prices. ARCHITECTURAL POINT: a value written every frame whose consumer wakes rarely, which is the shape of a virtualised list under scroll. Ours enlists the effect on the write, and at the flush the effect asks the index, which re-derives, finds the same value and stops. Alien-signals propagates pending flags to the computed and the effect on the write, and the effect checks the computed, which re-derives and stops. Browsers dispatch scroll at most once per rendered frame, so k1 is the scroll case; k4 is a handler that moves the position several times. Ours is @oimdb/core from source: an OIMSingleEntity root written through entityContentService.updateEntityColumn, OIMSingleComputed nodes for anything derived, one effect from OIMEffectService, and channel.flush() as the settle. The floor is alien-signals 3.2: signal, computed, effect, and startBatch/endBatch where the row says so. Every write stores a new number from a counter, so no write on either arm is stopped by a same-value check. Each arm runs in its own process.
